children: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD, Financials) is putting a much bigger number behind its AI ambitions. Shares climbed more than 6% Tuesday after the chipmaker told investors its data-center business could reach roughly $70 billion in revenue in 2027.
That would represent about a doubling of the business. AI accelerators are expected to do much of the work.
AMD said AI GPU revenue could reach the low-$40 billion range next year, supported by the MI450 ramp and customers including Meta Platforms, OpenAI and Anthropic.
Production shipments of the MI450 began in the third quarter, with a larger ramp expected in the fourth quarter and another increase in early 2027.
AMD also raised the long-term opportunity it sees in server CPUs. The company now estimates that market could reach $220 billion by 2030, up sharply from its previous $60 billion view.
That gives AMD two ways to benefit from AI infrastructure spending: accelerators and the CPUs surrounding them. There is a cost.

AMD said advanced wafers, high-bandwidth memory and packaging remain tight. The company has secured roughly $29 billion to $30 billion in purchase commitments to support the expansion. Margins could also take a temporary hit as MI450 production scales.
AMD expects gross margin to edge lower in the fourth quarter and into 2027, even as total gross profit dollars rise. That is the trade investors are making.

AMD is spending aggressively to capture a larger share of the AI market now. The next test will be whether the MI450 ramp can turn that spending into the kind of revenue growth AMD is forecasting for 2027.

title: AMD Just Put a $70 Billion Number on Its AI Ambitions
